text: Trace any function with weave.op, from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google AI Studio API calls to Hugging Face and open-source model generations
quote: You can trace any function using `weave.op` - from api calls to OpenAI, Anthropic, Google AI Studio etc to generation calls from Hugging Face and other open source models to any other validation functions or data transformations

text: Decorating or wrapping a function with weave.op in Python or TypeScript automatically captures its code, inputs, outputs, and execution metadata
quote: When you decorate a function with `@weave.op()` (Python) or wrap it with `weave.op()` (TypeScript), Weave automatically captures its code, inputs, outputs, and execution metadata.

text: Decorated functions produce a nested trace tree of the inputs and outputs of all traced functions
quote: Decorate all the functions you want to trace, this will generate a trace tree of the inputs and outputs of all your functions

text: Version application code and collect feedback about the application through manual instrumentation
quote: Manually instrument your application’s LLM calls and arbitrary functions to trace, version, and collect feedback about your application

text: Evaluate agent or application responses using LLM judges and custom scorers
quote: Evaluate your agent’s or application’s responses using LLM judges and custom scorers

text: Evaluate single-turn and multi-turn agents with the agents workflow and EvaluationLogger, scored by an LLM judge
quote: Evaluate single-turn and multi-turn AI agents in Weave using the agents workflow and EvaluationLogger, scored with an LLM judge.

text: Write custom scorers as @weave.op functions or as classes that inherit from weave.Scorer; scorers return a dictionary of metrics
quote: Function-based Scorers: Python functions decorated with @weave.op. Class-based Scorers: Python classes that inherit from weave.Scorer for more complex evaluations.

text: Evaluation object combines a dataset of test examples with one or more scoring functions
quote: the core of the workflow is the _`Evaluation` object_, which defines: A `Dataset` or list of dictionaries for test examples. One or more scoring functions.

text: Predefined and local SLM scorers for hallucination detection, summarization quality, and embedding similarity
quote: Weave comes with predefined scorers and local SLM scorers that you can use right away, including: Hallucination detection, Summarization quality, Embedding similarity

text: Guardrails provide pre-built safety scorers for toxicity, bias, PII detection, and hallucinations
quote: Weave Guardrails offers pre-built scorers for safety and quality to support responsible AI. Safety scorers include toxicity, bias, PII detection, and hallucinations

text: Compare and visualize evaluations to catch regressions between harness and model changes
quote: Measure every improvement to your harnesses and models with confidence with a flexible imperative evaluation API. Weave provides powerful evaluation comparisons and visualizations to catch regressions before they reach users

text: Run evaluations against repeatable test cases, compare changes over time, and identify regressions
quote: This guide shows you how to set up and run evaluations in Weave so you can measure your LLM application’s performance against repeatable test cases, compare changes over time, and identify regressions.

text: Test new LLMs and custom models against production traces for specific use cases
quote: You can test new LLMs and custom models against production traces, assessing their performance for your specific use cases.

text: Aggregate evaluations into leaderboards and share them across the organization
quote: Aggregate evaluations into leaderboards featuring the best performers and share them across your organization.

text: Playground supports prompt editing, message retrying, and model comparison for iterating on LLM apps
quote: With features like prompt editing, message retrying, and model comparison, Playground helps you test and improve your LLM applications.

text: Playground can test custom models served through OpenAI-compatible API endpoints
quote: Custom runtimes: Test OpenAI-compatible API endpoints for custom models.

text: Create and configure reusable saved model presets
quote: Saved models: Create and configure a reusable model preset for your workflow.

text: Automatically records token usage and cost for each call, shown in the trace tree and calls table
quote: Weave automatically records token usage and calculates cost for each call. Costs appear in the trace tree and in the calls table in the Weave UI.

text: Calling weave.init() auto-instruments supported LLM integrations such as OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere, and Mistral
quote: When you call weave.init() and use a supported LLM integration such as OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere, or Mistral, Weave automatically records token usage and calculates cost for each call.

text: Add custom per-token costs via add_cost for fine-tuned, self-hosted, or unsupported models
quote: Use custom cost tracking when automatic cost tracking isn’t available, such as with fine-tuned models, self-hosted models, or providers that Weave doesn’t integrate with.

text: Ingest OTLP-formatted trace data directly into a Weave project through a dedicated endpoint
quote: This endpoint lets you send OTLP (OpenTelemetry Protocol) formatted trace data directly to your Weave project.

text: OTel traces appear alongside other Weave data without replacing an existing OTel observability pipeline
quote: Use this integration when you want to instrument your application with the OpenTelemetry standard and have those traces appear alongside your other Weave data, without replacing your existing OTel-based observability pipeline.

text: Trace and collect metrics for agents built with popular SDKs and harnesses via an OTel-compatible SDK
quote: Trace and collect metrics about your agents built with popular SDKs and harnesses using Weave OTel-compatible SDK

text: OpenAI Agents SDK, Claude Agent SDK, and Google ADK are traced with just weave.init()
quote: OpenAI Agents SDK, Claude Agent SDK, and Google ADK. `weave.init()` is enough for those SDKs.

text: Instrument custom agent loops with start_conversation, start_turn, start_llm, and start_tool
quote: Custom agents — wrap your own loop with `start_conversation`, `start_turn`, `start_llm`, and `start_tool`.

text: Agent sessions, turns, steps, tools, and sub-agents are first-class concepts for navigating agent executions
quote: Weave now brings sessions, turns, steps, tools, and sub-agents as first-class concepts, making it much easier to navigate an agent session the way the agent actually executed it.

text: Threads group traces into a session or conversation so the whole conversation can be analyzed or scored
quote: Threads are collections of Traces related to a single session or conversation. You can use Threads to analyze or score the entire conversation instead of individual Calls.

text: Sessions-and-turns structure plus native analytics for tracing behavior across multi-agent systems
quote: Weave organizes traces into sessions and turns from the ground up. That structure, paired with native analytics tools, makes it easy to trace behavior across multi-agent systems

text: Calls and agent spans link to each other in both directions
quote: In Weave, calls and agent spans now link to each other in both directions.

text: REST Service API provides programmatic access to Weave functionality
quote: Use the Weave Service API, which provides REST endpoints for programmatic access to Weave functionality.

text: Built-in and custom signals automatically capture and classify agent interactions in production
quote: Built-in and custom signals automatically capture and classify agent interactions, so you always know how your agents are behaving.

text: Create custom signals that tag agent turns for a user-defined behavior
quote: Create a custom W\&B Weave signal to tag agent turns for a behavior you define.

text: Alerts send Slack notifications and trigger webhook automations
quote: Alerts route what matters through Slack notifications and trigger webhook automations, turning every production insight into a fast iteration.

text: Coding agents like Claude Code use W&B skills and the MCP server to read production data, run evals, and run automatic iteration loops
quote: Using W&B skills and the MCP server, coding agents like Claude Code connect to Weave. They can read live production data, run evaluations, and execute automatic iteration loops on their own

text: W&B MCP Server lets IDEs and agents answer questions about runs, traces, evaluations, and artifacts
quote: The W\&B MCP Server gives your IDE, coding assistant, or chat agent direct access to your W\&B data and documentation... your agent can answer questions about your runs, traces, evaluations, and artifacts without copy-paste.

text: Installable Skills teach agents to use the Weave SDK for traces, evaluations, and scorers
quote: Skills covers both the [W\&B Models SDK] ... and the [Weave SDK] (traces, evaluations, scorers).

text: Free $0/month plan includes AI application tracing, evaluations, and scorers
quote: Free ... $0/mo ... AI application evaluations ... AI application tracing ... AI application scorers
